# Winsock

Starting Winsock, address families, sockets and their options, and name resolution.

<h2 id="wsa-data"><code>WsaData</code></h2>

```rux
pub struct WsaData {
    // private fields
}
```

Room for a `WSADATA`, which [`WSAStartup`](/docs/api/windows/winsock#wsa-startup) fills and nothing here reads.

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Windows/Src/Winsock.rux#L7)

**Constructors**

```rux
pub func WsaData() -> WsaData
```

Zeroed storage for [`WSAStartup`](/docs/api/windows/winsock#wsa-startup) to fill.

**Returns**: the storage

<h2 id="address-info"><code>AddressInfo</code></h2>

```rux
pub struct AddressInfo {
    pub flags: int32;
    pub family: int32;
    pub socketType: int32;
    pub protocol: int32;
    pub addressLength: uint64;
    pub canonicalName: *char8;
    pub address: *opaque;
    pub next: *var AddressInfo;
}
```

Winsock's `addrinfo`: one result of [`getaddrinfo`](/docs/api/windows/winsock#getaddrinfo), linked to the next.

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Windows/Src/Winsock.rux#L22)

**Fields**

| Name            | Type               | Description                              |
| --------------- | ------------------ | ---------------------------------------- |
| `flags`         | `int32`            | Flags such as `AI_PASSIVE`.              |
| `family`        | `int32`            | The address family, or zero for any.     |
| `socketType`    | `int32`            | The socket type, or zero for any.        |
| `protocol`      | `int32`            | The protocol, or zero for any.           |
| `addressLength` | `uint64`           | The size of `address` in bytes.          |
| `canonicalName` | `*char8`           | The host's canonical name, or null.      |
| `address`       | `*opaque`          | The address, a `sockaddr`.               |
| `next`          | `*var AddressInfo` | The next result, or null after the last. |

<h2 id="ioctlsocket"><code>ioctlsocket</code></h2>

```rux
pub extern func ioctlsocket(
    socket: uint64,
    command: int32,
    argument: *var uint32
) -> int32
```

Sets a socket's mode, such as non-blocking with [`FIONBIO`](/docs/api/windows/winsock#fionbio).

**See also**: [https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/winsock/nf-winsock-ioctlsocket](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/winsock/nf-winsock-ioctlsocket)

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Windows/Src/Winsock.rux#L294)

**Parameters**

| Name       | Type          | Description                                                                                    |
| ---------- | ------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `socket`   | `uint64`      | the socket                                                                                     |
| `command`  | `int32`       | the mode to set, such as [`FIONBIO`](/docs/api/windows/winsock#fionbio)                        |
| `argument` | `*var uint32` | the mode's value: for [`FIONBIO`](/docs/api/windows/winsock#fionbio), nonzero for non-blocking |

**Returns**: zero, or -1 with the reason in [`WSAGetLastError`](/docs/api/windows/winsock#wsa-get-last-error)

<h2 id="wsa-poll"><code>WSAPoll</code></h2>

```rux
pub extern func WSAPoll(
    sockets: *var WsaPollFd,
    count: uint32,
    timeout: int32
) -> int32
```

Waits until one of `count` sockets is ready or `timeout` milliseconds pass, filling each one's `returned`.

**See also**: [https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/winsock2/nf-winsock2-wsapoll](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/winsock2/nf-winsock2-wsapoll)

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Windows/Src/Winsock.rux#L303)

**Parameters**

| Name      | Type             | Description                                                        |
| --------- | ---------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `sockets` | `*var WsaPollFd` | the sockets and the events wanted of each                          |
| `count`   | `uint32`         | how many there are                                                 |
| `timeout` | `int32`          | milliseconds to wait, zero to only look, or -1 to wait without end |

**Returns**: how many sockets have events, zero after the timeout, or -1 with the reason in [`WSAGetLastError`](/docs/api/windows/winsock#wsa-get-last-error)
